title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 2.1 The Inspired Word of God

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

The Holy Bible is God's inspired word. In this sub-strand you will learn to handle it with respect, name books in the Old Testament and the New Testament, and recite Isaiah 49:16. You will see why Christians want to read the Bible always.

## Strand 2.0: The Holy Bible
Sub-strand 2.1: The Inspired Word of God
Suggested lessons: 3

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 2.0 The Holy Bible, Sub-strand 2.1 The Inspired Word of God
• Isaiah 49:16

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) handle the Holy Bible with respect as the inspired word of God
b) identify the books in the Old and New Testament
c) role play naming some books in the Bible
d) recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why should you respect the Holy Bible?
2. Why is it important to know the books in the Holy Bible?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• sing a song related to respecting the Holy Bible
• role-play ways of handling the Holy Bible with respect
• in pairs, observe and read charts containing books in the Old and New Testament
• play games on naming some books in the Old and the New Testament
• recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16
• sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible

## Core competencies
• Collaboration: the skill of teamwork is enhanced as learners contribute to group discussions and take up different roles while singing and role playing.
• Creativity and imagination: the skill of originality is developed as learners come up with new ideas while playing games on naming some books in the Old and the New Testament.

## Values
• Responsibility: is enhanced as they learn how to care for the Holy Bible.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Spiritual Awareness: is enhanced as learners recite Isaiah 49:16

## Links to other learning areas
• Mathematics: counting skills are applied as learners count the number of books in the Holy Bible
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners play games on naming some Books in the Old and the New Testament
• English: reading skills are applied as learners read the Holy Bible

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: Handling the Holy Bible with respect

LESSON 1: HANDLING THE HOLY BIBLE WITH RESPECT
==============================================

## What you will learn
• Explain that the Holy Bible is the inspired word of God.
• Show ways of handling the Holy Bible with respect.

Curriculum outcomes: a) handle the Holy Bible with respect as the inspired word of God

## Introduction
At home you treat a gift from someone you love with care. The Holy Bible is a greater gift. It is God's word, so Christians handle it with respect.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: Handling the Holy Bible with respect — Why respect it

## Notes

The Holy Bible is the book of God's word. Inspired means that God guided the people who wrote it, so what it teaches is His message and not only human ideas. Because it is inspired, we do not treat it like a rough exercise book that we can tear or sit on.

### Why respect it
- It tells us who God is and what He has done.
- It shows us how to live.
- It contains the story of Jesus Christ and His teaching.
- It is the word Christians read in church, at home and at school.

Respecting the Bible is part of respecting God, who gave it.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: Handling the Holy Bible with respect — Ways to handle it

### Ways to handle it
- Wash your hands before you read, so the pages stay clean.
- Carry it carefully. Do not throw it or swing it.
- Do not place it on the floor or sit on it.
- Turn the pages gently. Do not fold or tear them.
- Do not draw jokes in it or use it to hit someone.
- Keep it in a clean, dry place when you finish.
- Mark a verse with a ribbon or a clean paper, not with food or a dirty stick.
- When it is being read, listen. Do not talk over the reader.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: Handling the Holy Bible with respect — Notes 4

Role-play these actions: one learner pretends to drop the Bible, and another shows the right way to pick it up and dust it with care. Sing a song about respecting the Holy Bible. Responsibility grows when you care for it every day, not only when the teacher is watching.

Reading it is the best respect. A Bible that is never opened is not being honoured. Open it, read a verse, and obey it.

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: Handling the Holy Bible with respect — Role-play respectful handling

## Key words
• Holy Bible — the inspired written word of God
• inspired — guided by God so that the writing is His word
• respect — to treat someone or something as valuable and worthy of care

## Activity: Role-play respectful handling
You will need: A Bible, A ribbon or clean paper for a bookmark

1. Sing a song related to respecting the Holy Bible.

2. In groups, role-play ways of handling the Bible with respect and ways that show disrespect.

3. The class says which actions are right.

4. Each learner shows how to open the Bible, find a page, and close it gently.

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: Handling the Holy Bible with respect — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What does it mean that the Bible is inspired?

2. Give three ways to handle the Holy Bible with respect.

3. Why should Christians respect the Holy Bible?

## Answers to practice

1. God guided the writers so that the Bible is His word.

2. Any three: clean hands, carry it carefully, do not put it on the floor, turn pages gently, do not tear it, store it safely, listen when it is read.

3. Because it is the inspired word of God.

## Summary
• The Holy Bible is the inspired word of God.
• Handle it gently, keep it clean, and do not throw or tear it.
• The greatest respect is to read it and obey it.

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: Books of the Old and New Testament

LESSON 2: BOOKS OF THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENT
============================================

## What you will learn
• Identify books in the Old Testament and the New Testament.
• Role-play and play games that name some Bible books.

Curriculum outcomes: b) identify the books in the Old and New Testament; c) role play naming some books in the Bible

## Introduction
The Bible is one book made of many smaller books. They are grouped into two main parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament. Knowing the names helps you find a verse when the teacher says "Luke" or "Genesis."

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: Books of the Old and New Testament — Notes 1

## Notes

A testament here is a covenant, a binding agreement between God and His people. The Old Testament tells of God's work before the birth of Jesus Christ. The New Testament tells of Jesus Christ and the first Christians.

The Old Testament has 39 books. The New Testament has 27 books. Together the Bible has 66 books.

### Some Old Testament books
The first five are Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. Other books you will meet in Grade 4 are Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, Psalms, Proverbs and Isaiah. The Old Testament also has books such as Joshua, Ruth, Job, Jeremiah and Malachi. Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Books of the Old and New Testament — How to tell them apart

### Some New Testament books
The first four are the Gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. They tell the life of Jesus. Acts comes next. Then there are letters, such as Romans, 1 Corinthians, Ephesians and Philippians. The last book is Revelation.

### How to tell them apart
If the story is about Abraham, Joseph, Samson, Balaam or the creation of the world, you are in the Old Testament. If the story is about the birth of Jesus, His miracles or His teaching in parables, you are in the New Testament.

### Naming games
In pairs, read a chart of the books. One learner calls "Old" or "New," and the partner names a book from that part. You can also role-play: hold a card that says "Exodus" or "John" and stand in the correct group. Counting the books uses the same careful counting you use in Mathematics. Knowing the names helps you respect the Bible by finding your place quickly.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Books of the Old and New Testament — Key words

## Key words
• Old Testament — the first part of the Bible, with 39 books, written before the birth of Jesus
• New Testament — the second part of the Bible, with 27 books, about Jesus and the first Christians
• Gospel — one of the four books that tell the life and teaching of Jesus: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John

## Worked examples

### Example 1
The teacher says, "Open Luke 19." Is Luke in the Old Testament or the New Testament?

Working:
1. Luke is one of the four Gospels.
2. The Gospels tell the life of Jesus.
3. They are in the New Testament.

Answer: Luke is in the New Testament.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: Books of the Old and New Testament — Chart reading and a naming game

## Activity: Chart reading and a naming game
You will need: Chart of Bible books, Cards with book names

1. In pairs, observe and read a chart of books in the Old and New Testament.

2. Count the Old Testament books and the New Testament books.

3. Play a game: a leader calls Old or New, and a learner names a book from that part.

4. Role-play naming books by holding a card and standing in the Old or New group.

5. Sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible.

PAGE 15: Lesson 2: Books of the Old and New Testament — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. How many books are in the Old Testament, the New Testament, and the whole Bible?

2. Name the four Gospels.

3. Is Genesis in the Old Testament or the New Testament?

4. Name two Old Testament books and two New Testament books.

## Answers to practice

1. 39 in the Old Testament, 27 in the New Testament, and 66 altogether.

2. Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

3. The Old Testament.

4. Any correct pair, for example Genesis and Psalms; Luke and Acts.

## Summary
• The Old Testament has 39 books and the New Testament has 27 books.
• The Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
• Games and charts help you name the books and find them quickly.

PAGE 16: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read

LESSON 3: ISAIAH 49:16 AND THE DESIRE TO READ
=============================================

## What you will learn
• Recite Isaiah 49:16.
• Give reasons for reading the Holy Bible always.

Curriculum outcomes: d) recite Isaiah 49:16 and desire to read the Holy Bible always

## Introduction
People write a name on a hand so they will not forget. God uses a picture like that in Isaiah 49:16. He does not forget His people. The Bible is where we keep meeting the God who remembers us.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read — Notes 1

## Notes

Isaiah 49:16 says that God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands. Their walls are always before Him. Engraved means cut or written so that it stays. God is telling His people that He cannot forget them. He keeps them in view, as if their name were written on His hand.

### Meditating on the verse
Read the verse slowly. Sit quietly. Think: God does not forget His people. I am one of the people He calls. He wants me to know Him. Recite the verse until you can say it without the book. This practice builds spiritual awareness, a heart that notices God.

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read — Why read the Bible always

### Why read the Bible always
- It is God's inspired word, so it tells the truth about Him.
- It reminds you that God does not forget you, as Isaiah 49:16 says.
- It shows the right way when you must make a choice.
- It introduces Jesus Christ, the Saviour.
- It gives verses to recite when you are afraid, angry or thankful.
- Reading every day keeps the habit alive. A verse a day is a good beginning.

Choose a regular time: after waking, or before you sleep. Keep the Bible where you can reach it. Ask a parent to listen while you read one short passage. When you desire to read always, you are treating the Bible as a friend you return to, not as a book you open only in an examination week.

Sing a song about the books of the Bible, then close by reciting Isaiah 49:16 together.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read — Recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16

## Key words
• engraved — written or cut in a lasting way
• meditate — to think quietly and carefully about a verse
• desire — a strong wish

## Activity: Recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16
You will need: Bible, Flash cards

1. Read Isaiah 49:16 aloud.

2. Write it on a flash card.

3. Recite it in pairs, then sit quietly and meditate on the promise that God does not forget His people.

4. Each learner says one reason for reading the Bible always.

5. Sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible.

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What picture does Isaiah 49:16 use?

2. What does engraved mean?

3. Give two reasons to read the Holy Bible always.

## Answers to practice

1. God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands, so He does not forget them.

2. Written or cut in a lasting way.

3. Any two: it is God's word; it reminds us God does not forget His people; it guides choices; it tells us about Jesus; it helps us when we are afraid or thankful.

## Summary
• Isaiah 49:16 says God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands.
• God does not forget His people.
• Christians desire to read the Bible always because it is His word.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The Holy Bible is called inspired because:
   A. learners wrote it in class
   B. God guided the writers so that it is His word
   C. it is the newest storybook
   D. it has no authors

2. Which action shows respect for the Bible?
   A. Sitting on it
   B. Throwing it on the floor
   C. Turning the pages gently
   D. Tearing a page to share

3. Why should you respect the Holy Bible?

4. How many books are in the New Testament?
   A. 27
   B. 39
   C. 12
   D. 66

5. Which book is in the Old Testament?
   A. Acts
   B. Romans
   C. Genesis
   D. Revelation

6. The four Gospels are...

7. A naming game in class helps learners to:
   A. hide the Bible
   B. name books in the Old and New Testament
   C. tear old pages
   D. avoid reading

8. Isaiah 49:16 teaches that God...
   A. forgets His people
   B. has engraved His people on the palms of His hands
   C. has no care for names
   D. only remembers kings

9. Why should you desire to read the Bible always?

10. The Old Testament has how many books?
   A. 27
   B. 39
   C. 66
   D. 5

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. B. God guided the writers so that it is His word
   Inspiration means God guided the writing of Scripture.

2. C. Turning the pages gently
   Gentle handling keeps the Bible clean and honours God's word.

3. Because it is the inspired word of God.
   Respect follows from knowing whose word it is.

4. A. 27
   The New Testament has 27 books. The Old Testament has 39. Together they make 66.

5. C. Genesis
   Genesis is the first book of the Old Testament.

6. Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
   These four New Testament books tell the life and teaching of Jesus.

7. B. name books in the Old and New Testament
   The learning experience includes games on naming Bible books.

8. B. has engraved His people on the palms of His hands
   The verse uses the picture of engraving so that God's people are not forgotten.

9. Because it is God's word and it helps me know Him, including His promise not to forget His people.
   Isaiah 49:16 and the inspiration of Scripture give reasons to keep reading.

10. B. 39
   There are 39 books in the Old Testament.

- It reminds you that God does not forget you, as Isaiah 49:16 says.
- It shows the right way when you must make a choice.
- It introduces Jesus Christ, the Saviour.
- It gives verses to recite when you are afraid, angry or thankful.
- Reading every day keeps the habit alive. A verse a day is a good beginning.

Choose a regular time: after waking, or before you sleep. Keep the Bible where you can reach it. Ask a parent to listen while you read one short passage. When you desire to read always, you are treating the Bible as a friend you return to, not as a book you open only in an examination week.

Sing a song about the books of the Bible, then close by reciting Isaiah 49:16 together.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read — Recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• engraved — written or cut in a lasting way
• meditate — to think quietly and carefully about a verse
• desire — a strong wish

## Activity: Recite and meditate on Isaiah 49:16
You will need: Bible, Flash cards

1. Read Isaiah 49:16 aloud.

2. Write it on a flash card.

3. Recite it in pairs, then sit quietly and meditate on the promise that God does not forget His people.

4. Each learner says one reason for reading the Bible always.

5. Sing a song about the books in the Holy Bible.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Isaiah 49:16 and the desire to read — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. What picture does Isaiah 49:16 use?

2. What does engraved mean?

3. Give two reasons to read the Holy Bible always.

## Answers to practice

1. God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands, so He does not forget them.

2. Written or cut in a lasting way.

3. Any two: it is God's word; it reminds us God does not forget His people; it guides choices; it tells us about Jesus; it helps us when we are afraid or thankful.

## Summary
• Isaiah 49:16 says God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands.
• God does not forget His people.
• Christians desire to read the Bible always because it is His word.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. The Holy Bible is called inspired because:
   A. learners wrote it in class
   B. God guided the writers so that it is His word
   C. it is the newest storybook
   D. it has no authors

2. Which action shows respect for the Bible?
   A. Sitting on it
   B. Throwing it on the floor
   C. Turning the pages gently
   D. Tearing a page to share

3. Why should you respect the Holy Bible?

4. How many books are in the New Testament?
   A. 27
   B. 39
   C. 12
   D. 66

5. Which book is in the Old Testament?
   A. Acts
   B. Romans
   C. Genesis
   D. Revelation

6. The four Gospels are...

7. A naming game in class helps learners to:
   A. hide the Bible
   B. name books in the Old and New Testament
   C. tear old pages
   D. avoid reading

8. Isaiah 49:16 teaches that God...
   A. forgets His people
   B. has engraved His people on the palms of His hands
   C. has no care for names
   D. only remembers kings

9. Why should you desire to read the Bible always?

10. The Old Testament has how many books?
   A. 27
   B. 39
   C. 66
   D. 5

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. B. God guided the writers so that it is His word
   Inspiration means God guided the writing of Scripture.

2. C. Turning the pages gently
   Gentle handling keeps the Bible clean and honours God's word.

3. Because it is the inspired word of God.
   Respect follows from knowing whose word it is.

4. A. 27
   The New Testament has 27 books. The Old Testament has 39. Together they make 66.

5. C. Genesis
   Genesis is the first book of the Old Testament.

6. Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
   These four New Testament books tell the life and teaching of Jesus.

7. B. name books in the Old and New Testament
   The learning experience includes games on naming Bible books.

8. B. has engraved His people on the palms of His hands
   The verse uses the picture of engraving so that God's people are not forgotten.

9. Because it is God's word and it helps me know Him, including His promise not to forget His people.
   Isaiah 49:16 and the inspiration of Scripture give reasons to keep reading.

10. B. 39
   There are 39 books in the Old Testament.
